requirements.text: Rename the existing span so it matches the contract exactly. expected `checkout.payment.authorize`, found `checkout.payment_authorize`. Do **not** add a new span — the instrumentation already exists and is emitting; only the name is wrong. This single change also satisfies the step requirement for that span.
A span named `checkout.confirmation_viewed` MUST be created in the browser runtime for step `confirmation_viewed`. Create it as a child of the surrounding span.

`checkout.outcome` MUST be a string enum (completed | failed | abandoned | rejected), not a boolean. Sentry renders boolean attributes as the strings 'true'/'false', so the current value cannot express more than two states.
`checkout.outcome` MUST be initialised to `abandoned` when the journey starts and overwritten on a terminal event.

When the outcome is not a success value, the span MUST carry `payment.decline_reason` with the provider's or system's **coded** reason. Known values: insuffic_funds, do_not_honor, 3ds_required, gateway_timeout. Never a free-text message, never a raw upstream payload.
The span for step `order_created` MUST carry `order.value` as a **double** (a JavaScript number, not a string).
`cart.value` is type `string`, expected `number`. It MUST be emitted as a number. A stringified value cannot be aggregated — `sum()` and `p50()` return nothing useful while the code looks correct.
Existing `Sentry.init()` options, sampling rates, and unrelated instrumentation MUST NOT be modified.
No PII, card data, token, or raw provider payload may appear in any span name, `op`, or attribute.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given one completed journey, when I search spans for `checkout.id` matching that instance, then all 7 spans in §2 are present.
Given any completed journey, when I filter on `checkout.outcome`, then every instance resolves to exactly one value.
Given the rename is complete, when I search for the old span name, then no new spans appear under it.
Given completed journeys, when I query `sum(cart.value)`, then a numeric result renders — proving the attribute was stored as a number.
Given a failed journey, when I group spans by `payment.decline_reason`, then every result has a non-empty coded reason.
Given the journey crosses runtimes, when I open a trace for the hand-off step, then spans from both runtimes appear in the same trace.
Given any span in this journey, when I inspect all attributes, then no PII, card data, or raw provider payload is present.
